notes.title: Ruthless, overlooked FPS game is cheaper than ever at $5, with a sequel incoming
notes.notes:
Robocop: Rogue City is, on paper, the exact opposite style to my favorite shooters. I adore fast-paced, frenetic, and movement-based games where my skill is measured by how quickly (and stylishly) I can act. I'm talking about the likes of Neon White, Titanfall, and Ultrakill. Rogue City, on the other hand, is all about being slow and methodical. You can't run and gun, but you can dominate a shootout simply by standing there and picking off goons one-by-one. As an encapsulation of the movies, it's nothing short of superb, and you can now experience it yourself for the cheapest it's ever been on Steam.

notes.title: RoboCop: Rogue City - Unfinished Business Story Trailer
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=_bep-j3cEmQ;full][/previewyoutube]
Welcome back to Old Detroit,

Unfinished Business picks up where Rogue City left off. While RoboCop continues policing the streets, OCP are working on a new project, the OmniTower, a housing complex designed for the residents evicted from their homes as the corporation proceeds to make way for Delta City.

A group of mercenaries tears into the Metro West precinct, leaving after stealing components from RoboCop's medical chair. Their next target, the OmniTower. The tower can serve as a potential power source, which, combined with those stolen components, would give the mercenaries access to all OCP's technology, including RoboCop.

Pulling off this plan will take time, so they've seized control of the tower, turning each floor into a dangerous maze of enemies, traps, and bullets that you'll have to contend with if you want to retain control of yourself.

As you ascend the tower, ghosts from Alex Murphy’s past will come back to haunt him. The leader of the mercenaries is a former colleague of Murphy. These two's goals are the same, protecting Old Detroit, but their motives differ.

Uncover these motives on July 17th in RoboCop: Rogue City - Unfinished Business. Wishlist for a reminder on release!

notes.title: Vicious and smart, one of PC's top hidden-gem FPS games is cheaper than ever
notes.notes:
In Doom Eternal, you have to sprint, leap, and pirouette to stay alive and get the drop on the hellspawn. In Half-Life and Half-Life 2, it's all about keeping your HEV suit charged and, especially during the many platforming and physics-based puzzle sections, watching your step and proceeding with extreme caution. In most FPS games, you have to be either precise and skillful or slow and careful. Robocop Rogue City is the total opposite. You're a machine. You're a tank. Grab a 12 gauge, march right in there, and blast bad guys at your robotic leisure. With a new DLC just announced, one of the top hidden-gem shooters on Steam is now the cheapest it's ever been.

notes.notes:
RoboCop will be climbing an apartment tower full of slimebags in a standalone follow-up to his trudging but faithful 2023 shooter. Robocop: Rogue City - Unfinished Business is so over-named it looks like DLC, but is actually an independent sequel from the same developers, and directly follows the events of the recent criminal justice 'em up. It'll see metal man Murphy going floor to floor as he and other Detroit city policefolk ascend a residential tower after "a group of highly trained mercenaries armed with cutting-edge weapons takes control of the building and turns it into their deadly fortress." notes.title: One of the most overlooked and underrated FPS games is finally back
notes.notes:
What I like best about Robocop Rogue City is how it functions as a kind of 'anti FPS.' Normally in shooters, as well as doling out the punishment, you've got to move fast and make use of cover, but in Rogue City, you're literally Robocop. There is a health bar and you can die, but the dynamic is completely flipped - imagine a dungeon raid in an RPG, or an endgame boss fight, except you're the boss. One of the biggest sleeper hits in Steam history, after more than a year of silence, Robocop Rogue City is finally back with a new standalone expansion, the aptly titled Unfinished Business.

notes.title: Robocop Rogue City is a superb FPS, and now the dev has something new
notes.notes:
Counter-Strike 2 and Starfield were the two biggest FPS games - or FPS and RPG mashups - of 2023. Going up against Valve and Bethesda, it's not surprising that plucky shooter Robocop Rogue City slipped under the radar, but if you haven't played it already, please do. Funny, vicious, and original, Rogue City is one of the most underrated shooters in years. Created by Teyon, maker of the similarly overlooked Terminator Resistance, Rogue City proves the studio has a skill for FPS design. But its new project sounds very different, and perhaps closer to the likes of Diablo 4 and Path of Exile.

notes.title: The Last of Us gets massive frame rate boost, thanks to AMD
notes.notes:
In the ongoing crusade to get AMD FSR 3 into as many games as possible, three new titles have been announced, with one being a very welcome addition. The Last of Us Part 1 has unfortunately seen its PC port struggle with performance issues since launch, and the inclusion of AMD's latest upscaling and frame generation tech should be a savior of sorts for those without an Nvidia RTX GPU.

Even if you have the best graphics card, game performance can still sometimes be a little behind where you want it to be. This could be for several reasons, but ultimately it's upscaling and frame generation tech like AMD FSR 3 and Nvidia DLSS that can provide the needed frame boost.

notes.title: New Game+ & more!

We're glad to not only announce, but also launch a new major update for RoboCop: Rogue City!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847542/fb203c60951a5a3527c733d9727c2dcf7cde0cc9.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Devblog: An Epic Story in the RoboCop Universe
notes.notes:
When we embarked on the ambitious task of creating an original story set in the beloved RoboCop universe, one fundamental question drove our creative process: Why tell THIS story?" We discovered not one but [b]two compelling reasons that fuelled our passion for this project[/b].

First and foremost, as devoted fans, we couldn't ignore the intriguing gaps that existed between the second and third movies. There was the untold story of what led to the Japanese firm Kanemitsu Corporation’s acquisition of Detroit's powerful conglomerate OCP. Then there was the fate of OCP’s enigmatic chairman and antagonist, the Old Man. Furthermore, the repercussions of the events portrayed in the second movie remained a mystery. We felt we were able to fill in these gaps, which compelled us to set our story between the second and third films.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847542/0a9874449a7cee6ce1e17524dcb28aa587a92555.jpg[/img]
But there was [b]more to it than just filling in gaps in the timeline[/b]. The timeless themes explored in the RoboCop movies resonated with us on a profound level. Themes such as loss, sacrifice, the defence of the vulnerable, and the dire consequences of selfishness and greed have always been intrinsic elements of the franchise. We wanted to delve deeper into these themes and make them central to our story.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847542/af2448f130d1cb562673f106bc0ac36b45bf85a9.jpg[/img]
To accomplish this, [b]we incorporated both familiar and new characters[/b] into our narrative canvas. While RoboCop has always been a lone wolf, he's had unique allies around him. We decided to bring these beloved characters into our game alongside some original ones. 

Police officers like Anne Lewis illustrate the true meaning of sacrifice in the fight for justice, and the inclusion of an intrepid reporter adds depth to our storytelling.

We also added a young boy who has tragically lost his father and is an eager recruit yearning for recognition. Through these characters we explored the theme of fatherhood, something that was taken away from Alex Murphy.

Our story wouldn't be complete without a good-hearted criminal seeking redemption, which explores the theme of who deserves a second chance.

But it wasn't just the heroes; we also crafted new villains who challenge our perception of humanity and at what point a person ceases to be human.

In RoboCop: Rogue City, players interact with these characters and have the power to change their destinies, for better or worse. These choices permanently shape the game world and leave it in a different state than how they found it.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847542/e0fec4444e7fe36b0ce4dbdc6cc9bbae2e60fd11.jpg[/img]
We recognized that[b] a RoboCop story should be a satirical yet cautionary tale at its core[/b]. It should effortlessly blend retro sci-fi vibes with the gritty elements of a crime drama. We have carefully crafted a story that we believe seamlessly integrates into the RoboCop universe and potentially answers questions that have lingered unanswered for some time.

We have taken familiar elements and woven them together with new ones, creating an exhilarating 80s-style adventure. But beyond the adrenaline-pumping action, our narrative transforms into a thought-provoking police drama, enriched with sci-fi elements, which asks players to confront ethical dilemmas and allows them to arrive at their own answers. In "Rogue City," you won't just play a game; you'll embark on an epic journey through the rich and ever-evolving world of RoboCop.


RoboCop: Rogue City is set to release on 2 November 2023 and is available for preorder on Steam. Stay up to date with the latest news, developer blogs and trailers by following us on Twitter or joining our official Discord server.

When is the RoboCop Rogue City release date? While the RoboCop franchise is no stranger to game tie-ins, they were all basic run-and-gun shooters of varying quality. Rogue City is more than that: an exploration of the dilapidated drug-fueled future city of Old Detroit through the lens of the 1980s, where corporate entities try to solve crime with experimental technology, with varying degrees of success.

As technology in the real world evolves, more complex games are commonplace, and RoboCop Rogue City seemingly attempts to do what was impossible during the late 1980s. This police game has players assume control of RoboCop, either enforcing the law to the letter or gaining the public's trust. It even shares similarities to RPG games, such as Fallout with its morality system. notes.title: RoboCop: Rogue City - Gameplay Reveal
notes.notes:
Welcome to Detroit; crime runs rampant as the city lies on the edge of ruin, people fighting for scraps as others live extravagant lives of luxury. Control of the Detroit Police Department is given to the Omni Consumer Products corporation in an attempt to restore order. You are that solution, RoboCop, a cyborg tasked with protecting the city. 

[h2]Watch the Gameplay Reveal[/h2]
[previewyoutube=jQ2hZ-4JCTE;full][/previewyoutube]
The triumphant return of RoboCop wouldn’t feel right without the man who brought so much life into the role, and we’re excited to reveal that [b]Peter Weller[/b] will be performing voice-over work on the game. Enjoy this first look at gameplay and for the record, “dead or alive, you’re coming with me!” 

RoboCop: Rogue City will be coming to Steam in June 2023.

notes.title: RoboCop is getting a videogame in 2023
notes.notes:
The Nacon Direct show today had a surprise reveal: an all new RoboCop game. The presentation featured a quick reveal teaser for RoboCop: Rogue City, which is currently in development and slated for a release some time in 2023. We get a quick glimpse of Old Detroit, a reference to OCP, and a peek at RoboCop's leg holster opening up to reveal his trusty service pistol.

RoboCop: Rogue City promises to be a "new story" based on the three RoboCop films, which tell the story of Detroit police officer Alex Murphy and his transformation from injured cop to unstoppable crime-fighting machine. Brazenly satirical of the consumerism and excess of the late 1980s, the first two RoboCop films in particular are classics of the period's science fiction genre and have remained cult classics to this day.

There's little information available about RoboCop: Rogue City, however. Nacon will publish the game, which may be an open-world game or FPS game, and it's being developed by Teyon, the studio responsible for Rambo: The Video Game and Terminator: Resistance.

notes.title: There's a new RoboCop game in the works from the team behind Terminator: Resistance
notes.notes:
It's been quite some time since iconic 80s action-movie antihero RoboCop had a video game to call his own (he last appeared on PC and consoles over 18 years ago, re-emerging with a free-to-play mobile offering in 2014), but it's been revealed everybody's favourite cyborg security professional will be making a long-awaited gaming comeback in RoboCop: Rogue City.

RoboCop: Rogue City, which is set for release on PC and currently unannounced consoles some time in 2023, is the work of developer Teyon (the studio responsible for the critically savaged Terminator: Resistance and Rambo: The Video Game), and will feature an "original story" based on the events of the first three RoboCop films.

Beyond the fact that players will take on the role of RoboCop himself - "Become the iconic hero whose [sic] part man, part machine, all cop as you attempt to bring justice to the dangerous, crime-ridden streets of Old Detroit in RoboCop: Rogue City," teases publisher Nacon in its press release - specifics are currently a little scarce.
